title: BVA Decision 25000008
text:
Citation Nr: 25000008
Decision Date: 01/02/25	Archive Date: 01/02/25

DOCKET NO. 18-04 499
DATE: January 2, 2025

REMANDED

The claim of entitlement to service connection for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is remanded.

REASONS FOR REMAND

The Veteran served on active duty from March 1963 to March 1965.

This matter comes to the Board of Veterans' Appeals (Board) on appeal of a rating decision by a Regional Office (RO) of the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

The claim is remanded. 

This case has been subject to multiple actions by the Board and by the U.S. Court of Appeal for Veterans Claims (Court). Most recently, in September 2024, the Board remanded the matter for additional medical inquiry pursuant to a Court remand in August 2023.

Unfortunately, an additional remand is needed. The United States Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (Court) has held that a permanent worsening of a non-service-connected disability is not required to establish secondary service connection on the basis of aggravation (i.e., aggravation may include temporary worsening of a disability).  See Ward v. Wilkie, 31 Vet. App. 233, 239-40 (2019).  The prior Board remand requested a secondary opinion as to the Veteran's COPD disorder as secondary to his service-connected lung cancer. 

The responding opinion for aggravation addresses why the Veteran's COPD has not been permanently aggravated by his lung cancer.  However, the opinion also suggests that the Veteran's COPD was temporarily aggravated by his lung cancer. Specifically, the opinion indicates that the Veteran "developed pneumothorax during resection of his lung cancer in 2016."  While the opinion indicates that the pneumothorax resolved, it does not explain why this was not a temporary worsening of his COPD due to his lung cancer. 

As whether or not aggravation, temporary or permanent worsening, has occurred was part of the Board's prior remand directives, a remand is needed to ensure adequate compliance.  See Stegall v. West, 11 Vet. App. 268, 271 (1998) (holding veterans are entitled to compliance with Board remand instructions). 

The Board acknowledges the Sergeant First Class Heath Robinson Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics Act of 2022 (PACT Act) provides that a TERA medical examination/opinion is required in cases of toxic-exposed veterans where there is a claim for a disability that is not clearly due to an etiology not associated with toxic exposure (such as in cases of physical trauma or mental disorders), and the evidence is not otherwise sufficient to establish service connection for the disability.  See 38 U.S.C. §§ 101 (38); 1168(a), 1710(e)(1)., Pub. L. 117-168, § 303 (to be codified at 38 U.S.C. § 1168).  Yet, the Secretary of VA has determined that there is no positive association between exposure to herbicide agents and COPD.  See VBA Letter 20-22-10, Processing Claims Involving the PACT Act, 87 Fed. Reg. 78,543 (Dec. 22, 2022) (detailing the four situations in which VA currently finds no indication of an association between the claimed disability and a TERA).  As such, the Board finds that a VA examination for toxic exposure risk activity on the basis of herbicide exposure is not warranted. 

However, the Veteran has also asserted toxic exposures to asbestos insulation.  As a result, the Board infers from the Veteran's claim that he has raised the issue of a toxic exposure risk activity (TERA) with respect to asbestos. The sub-regulatory guidance to the PACT Act states that both explicit and implicit claims include claims related to garrison exposures, which are any environmental exposure experienced while stationed on a military base including asbestos.  Accordingly, the Board finds that a TERA opinion is required as provided for under the PACT Act for the Veteran's COPD. 

The matters are REMANDED for the following action:

1. In rendering the requested opinion, the examiner must address and consider (1) the total potential toxic exposure through the Veteran's military deployment and (2) the synergistic, combined effect of all toxic exposure risk activities of the Veteran.

2. Return the case to VA examiner who issued the October 2024 VA reports, or to a suitable substitute, for issuance of an addendum medical opinion.  After reviewing the claims file, the examiner should address the following question(s):

(a.) Opine as to whether it is at least as likely as not (i.e. a 50 percent or greater probability) that the Veteran's COPD had its onset during, or is otherwise related to, his active-duty service, to include claimed asbestos exposure?

In rendering the requested opinion, the examiner must address and consider (1) the total potential toxic exposure through the Veteran's military deployment and (2) the synergistic, combined effect of all toxic exposure risk activities of the Veteran.

(b.) Is it approximately at least as likely as not that COPD has been aggravated (i.e., temporarily or permanently worsened) by service-connected lung cancer?

The evidentiary standard "at least as likely as not" is defined as the "likelihood is at least approximately balanced or nearly equal, if not higher." Conversely, "less likely than not" is defined as the "likelihood is less than approximately balanced or nearly equal."

In rendering the requested opinions, the examiner should note that the Veteran is competent to attest to matters of which he has first-hand knowledge, including observable symptomatology.

In remanding this case, the Board makes no credibility determination, expressed or implied, at this juncture.

?

Please explain in detail any opinion provided and the supporting rationale.

If the examiner cannot provide an opinion without resorting to mere speculation, he or she shall provide a complete explanation for why an opinion cannot be rendered.  In so doing, the examiner shall explain whether the inability to provide a more definitive opinion is the result of a need for additional information, or that he or she has exhausted the limits of current medical knowledge in providing an answer to that particular question(s).

 

 

G. A. WASIK

Veterans Law Judge

Board of Veterans' Appeals

Attorney for the Board	J. Wade, Counsel

The Board's decision in this case is binding only with respect to the instant matter decided. This decision is not precedential and does not establish VA policies or interpretations of general applicability. 38 C.F.R. § 20.1303.
